910.name: Hallstatt Celtic Culture & Roman Noricum
910.description: The Hallstatt culture represents one of Europe's earliest identifiable Celtic civilisations, centred in the salt-mining region of upper Austria. The subsequent Roman province of Noricum became a vital frontier territory supplying iron and gold to the empire.

sub_clusters.name: Hallstatt Salt-Mining Culture
sub_clusters.description: The early Iron Age Hallstatt culture, characterised by elite burials, salt extraction, and long-distance trade networks across Central Europe.
key_events: Discovery of Hallstatt cemetery with over 1,000 burials
Peak of trans-Alpine salt trade networks c. 600 BCE

sub_clusters.name: Roman Province of Noricum
sub_clusters.description: Incorporation of the Celtic Norican kingdom into the Roman Empire, development of Carnuntum as a major legionary fortress, and eventual collapse during the Migration Period.

920.name: Babenberg Dynasty & Medieval Austria
920.description: The Babenberg margraves and dukes transformed the eastern march (Ostarrîchi) into a prosperous duchy, fostering Crusade participation, monastic culture, and the Minnesang tradition.

sub_clusters.name: Ostarrîchi Margraviate
sub_clusters.description: Establishment of the March of Austria under the Babenbergs, first documented as 'Ostarrîchi' in the 996 deed, and its elevation to a duchy in the Privilegium Minus of 1156.
key_events: First written mention of 'Ostarrîchi' in 996 CE
Privilegium Minus elevates Austria to a duchy (1156)

sub_clusters.name: Babenberg Crusade Era & Late Dynasty
sub_clusters.description: Austrian participation in the Crusades, Duke Leopold V's capture of Richard the Lionheart, and the extinction of the Babenberg line with Frederick the Quarrelsome.

920.name: Early Habsburg Rise
920.description: Rudolf I's election as King of the Romans in 1273 launched the Habsburg dynasty's extraordinary ascent, establishing Austria as the family's hereditary power base and nucleus for a future world empire.

sub_clusters.name: Rudolf I & Habsburg Foundations
sub_clusters.description: Rudolf I's defeat of Ottokar II at the Battle on the Marchfeld (1278), acquisition of Austria and Styria, and the forged Privilegium Maius asserting Austrian pre-eminence.
key_events: Battle on the Marchfeld secures Habsburg control of Austria (1278)

sub_clusters.name: Habsburg Dynastic Marriage Strategy
sub_clusters.description: The famous policy of 'Bella gerant alii, tu felix Austria nube' – Habsburg expansion through strategic marriages linking Austria to Burgundy, Spain, and Hungary.

930.name: Ottoman Wars & Reformation Era
930.description: Austria's dual struggle against Ottoman expansion and Protestant Reformation, culminating in the dramatic sieges of Vienna and the Counter-Reformation's triumph under Ferdinand II.

sub_clusters.name: First Ottoman Siege of Vienna
sub_clusters.description: Following the Ottoman victory at Mohács (1526), Suleiman the Magnificent besieged Vienna in 1529. The city's successful defence marked the high-water mark of Ottoman expansion into Central Europe.
key_events: Battle of Mohács and fall of Hungary (1526)
First Siege of Vienna by Suleiman the Magnificent (1529)

sub_clusters.name: Counter-Reformation & Thirty Years' War
sub_clusters.description: Ferdinand II's aggressive re-Catholicisation of Habsburg lands, the Defenestration of Prague, and Austria's central role in the devastating Thirty Years' War.

sub_clusters.name: Second Ottoman Siege of Vienna (1683)
sub_clusters.description: The 1683 siege by Kara Mustafa Pasha, the decisive relief by Jan III Sobieski's cavalry charge, and the subsequent Habsburg reconquest of Hungary sealed by the Treaty of Karlowitz.
key_events: Battle of Vienna – Sobieski's cavalry charge breaks the siege (1683)
Treaty of Karlowitz ends Ottoman threat to Central Europe (1699)

940.name: Maria Theresa & Enlightened Absolutism
940.description: The reign of Maria Theresa and Joseph II transformed Austria through centralising reforms, compulsory education, religious toleration, and cultural brilliance epitomised by Mozart's Vienna.

sub_clusters.name: War of the Austrian Succession
sub_clusters.description: Maria Theresa's fight to defend her inheritance against Frederick the Great's seizure of Silesia, reshaping the European balance of power.

sub_clusters.name: Theresian & Josephine Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Sweeping administrative, educational, and religious reforms under Maria Theresa and Joseph II, including abolition of serfdom, Patent of Toleration, and codification of law.
key_events: Maria Theresa introduces compulsory primary education (1774)
Joseph II issues the Patent of Toleration (1781)

940.name: Congress of Vienna & Metternich Era
940.description: Austria's central role in the Napoleonic Wars, Metternich's orchestration of the post-war European order at the Congress of Vienna, and the conservative system's eventual collapse in the Revolutions of 1848.

sub_clusters.name: Napoleonic Wars & Congress of Vienna
sub_clusters.description: Austria's repeated wars against revolutionary and Napoleonic France, the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire (1806), and Metternich's masterful diplomacy at the Congress of Vienna (1814–15).
key_events: Dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire (1806)

sub_clusters.name: Revolutions of 1848 & Aftermath
sub_clusters.description: The March Revolution in Vienna, Metternich's flight, the rise of Franz Joseph I, and Austria's defeat by Prussia at Königgrätz (1866) ending its German leadership.

940.name: Austro-Hungarian Dual Monarchy
940.description: The Ausgleich of 1867 created the Dual Monarchy, a multi-ethnic empire struggling with nationalist tensions, Balkan ambitions, and the cultural flowering of fin-de-siècle Vienna.

sub_clusters.name: Ausgleich & Dual Monarchy Structure
sub_clusters.description: The Compromise of 1867 establishing separate Austrian and Hungarian governments under Franz Joseph, and the empire's management of its diverse nationalities.

sub_clusters.name: Fin-de-Siècle Vienna & Balkan Crisis
sub_clusters.description: Vienna as a cultural capital (Klimt, Freud, Mahler, Wittgenstein), the annexation of Bosnia-Herzegovina (1908), and rising South Slav tensions leading to Sarajevo.
key_events: Assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand at Sarajevo (28 June 1914)

950.name: World War I & Imperial Collapse
950.description: Austria-Hungary's catastrophic decision to issue the July Ultimatum to Serbia triggered the Great War, which destroyed the empire and left a diminished Austrian republic.

sub_clusters.name: WWI & Habsburg Collapse
sub_clusters.description: Austria-Hungary's war on multiple fronts, the death of Franz Joseph (1916), and the empire's disintegration into successor states in October–November 1918.

sub_clusters.name: First Republic Foundation
sub_clusters.description: Proclamation of the Republic of German-Austria, the Treaty of Saint-Germain stripping territories and forbidding Anschluss, and the new constitution of 1920.

950.name: Anschluss, WWII & Allied Occupation
950.description: The descent into Austrofascism, Nazi annexation in 1938, Austrian participation in WWII and the Holocaust, and the post-war decade of four-power Allied occupation ending with the State Treaty.

sub_clusters.name: Austrofascism & the Anschluss
sub_clusters.description: Dollfuss's authoritarian Fatherland Front, the failed Nazi putsch (1934), Schuschnigg's capitulation, and Hitler's triumphant entry into Vienna on 15 March 1938.

sub_clusters.name: WWII & the Holocaust in Austria
sub_clusters.description: Austrian integration into the Third Reich, the Mauthausen concentration camp, Austrian resistance movements, and liberation by Allied forces in 1945.

sub_clusters.name: Allied Occupation & Austrian State Treaty
sub_clusters.description: Four-zone occupation of Austria, denazification, economic reconstruction, and the landmark Austrian State Treaty of 1955 restoring full sovereignty on condition of perpetual neutrality.
key_events: Austrian State Treaty signed – sovereignty restored, neutrality declared (1955)

960.name: Neutral Austria & European Integration
960.description: Austria's path from Cold War neutrality to EU membership, including the Waldheim affair, Haider's far-right challenge, and Austria's role as a bridge between East and West.

sub_clusters.name: Cold War Neutrality & Bridge Role
sub_clusters.description: Austria as a neutral meeting ground during the Cold War, hosting international organisations in Vienna, the Waldheim controversy, and response to the Hungarian and Czech crises.

sub_clusters.name: EU Membership & Modern Politics
sub_clusters.description: Austria's EU accession (1995), the diplomatic sanctions triggered by Haider's FPÖ entering government (2000), the refugee crisis (2015), and ongoing debates over neutrality and far-right populism.
key_events: EU diplomatic sanctions over FPÖ coalition government (2000)

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
